name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals NeuroPrecision Surgical BCI
description:
The NeuroPrecision Surgical BCI is a medical-grade neural interface developed by LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS specifically for surgeons, microsurgeons, and high-precision medical specialists operating in environments where sub-millimeter accuracy is non-negotiable. The implant integrates a proprietary Tremor Elimination Matrix (TEM) that intercepts efferent motor signals before they reach the hands and fingers, filtering out physiological micro-tremors with a latency of less than 8 milliseconds — effectively granting the user hands that do not shake regardless of fatigue, stress, caffeine load, or emotional state. Beyond tremor suppression, the NeuroPrecision overlays a real-time haptic feedback amplification layer that enhances tactile sensitivity in the fingertips by a factor of 12x, allowing surgeons to detect tissue density variations, vessel walls, and implant seating resistance that would be imperceptible to unaugmented hands. An integrated surgical AR overlay syncs with operating theater systems to project anatomical mapping, instrument tracking, and patient vital flags directly onto the user's visual cortex without external headgear.

The NeuroPrecision is the gold standard of surgical augmentation in GLMZ's licensed medical sector, and possession of one is virtually synonymous with elite surgical credentials. Teaching hospitals in the upper Canopy tiers issue them to residents upon completion of their first fellowship year, and the implant's serial number is registered with the Meridian Medical Licensing Authority as part of the surgeon's professional record. Outside the OR, NeuroPrecision users are notable for an almost uncanny stillness of hand — a social tell that other medical professionals recognize instantly. A small but significant underground market exists among artisans, jewelers, tattoo artists, and forgers who obtain grey-market NeuroPrecision units for the tremor suppression and haptic amplification alone.
installation_requirements: Installation by licensed neurosurgeon in certified medical facility; Meridian Medical Licensing Authority registration required; 2-week supervised motor calibration post-installation
rejection_risk: Minimal — Lazarus biocompatible polymer chassis with pharmaceutical-grade anti-inflammatory nanolace; rejection events extremely rare, documented primarily in patients with pre-existing autoimmune conditions
maintenance: Bi-annual TEM recalibration by Lazarus-certified medical technician; firmware updates pushed automatically via Meridian Medical Network; haptic sensitivity tuning adjustable via licensed companion app

side_effects: Phantom precision syndrome — users report feeling as though their hands are 'too still' in non-surgical contexts, creating mild dissociative awareness of their own motor function
Haptic sensitivity overflow in high-stimulus environments: crowded spaces, rough fabrics, and handshakes can feel overwhelming without manual sensitivity dampening engaged
Dependency risk: approximately 19% of long-term users report degraded unaugmented fine motor confidence, feeling unable to perform precision work without the implant active
Rare: AR overlay persistence — surgical mapping ghosts occasionally bleeding into normal vision during periods of high cognitive load
cultural_context: Among GLMZ's medical elite, the NeuroPrecision is worn with quiet pride — it is never advertised, never discussed in polite company, and universally recognized. Surgical residents in upper-Canopy teaching hospitals speak of 'earning their Laz' the way earlier generations spoke of receiving a medical license. The grey-market artisan use of the implant has created a fascinating cultural crossover: a Tier 2 tattoo artist operating out of a Shelf-adjacent studio with a black-market NeuroPrecision can command Tier 4 prices for their work, and several such artists have built cult followings. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals formally disapproves of non-medical use but has never successfully prosecuted an artisan under their licensing terms.

story_hooks: A renowned black-market surgeon with a NeuroPrecision has gone missing; their implant's medical network ping has gone dark, and both Lazarus Pharmaceuticals and a criminal organization are looking for them — for very different reasons

A player needs a piece of evidence extracted from a corpse without triggering the forensic tamper-seal; the only person with the skill to do it is an artisan forger running a grey-market NeuroPrecision in a Tier 2 back-alley studio

A hospital's entire surgical wing is being held hostage; the lead surgeon's NeuroPrecision has been remotely tampered with via a spoofed Lazarus firmware update, and unless someone can isolate the malware, every patient on the operating tables is at risk
